title: Global Trends 2040: A More Contested World
notes: Cover date March 2021; public release 8 April 2021 (the Wayback Machine's first capture of the PDF is 2021-04-08). Seventh edition. Scope: the five scenarios for 2040 (quoted from the overview cards, pp. 4-5) and dated or quantified projections the NIC states in its own voice in the Executive Summary and the 'Structural Forces' chapters (demographics, economics, technology) and 'International Dynamics'. Regional annex tables (five largest cities by 2035, climate maps for 2040) are charts and are not captured. Figures the NIC attributes to others (OECD fragile-contexts 2.2 billion by 2030; World Economic Forum automation jobs by 2025; 'some estimates' of 64 billion IoT devices by 2025; UN city and population projections) are excluded. Several pages are set in two or three columns; pdftotext interleaves them, so some quotes stop at a column break. Scenario narratives contain dated fictional events (for example China the largest economy by 2030 in Competitive Coexistence); these are scenario content, not projections, and are not captured. dni.gov returns 403 to scripts; read from the Wayback copy.

entries.label: Renaissance of Democracies
entries.quote: The world is in the midst of a resurgence of open democracies led by the United States and its allies.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Overview card, p. 4. Technology from US-led public-private partnerships transforms the economy; controls in China and Russia stifle innovation.

entries.label: A World Adrift
entries.quote: The international system is directionless, chaotic, and volatile as international rules and institutions are largely ignored.
entries.subject: global order
entries.note: Overview card, p. 5. OECD countries stagnate and divide; China expands influence but does not lead globally.

entries.label: Competitive Coexistence
entries.quote: The United States and China have prioritized economic growth and restored a robust trading relationship, but this economic interdependence exists alongside competition over political influence, governance models, technological dominance, and strategic advantage.
entries.subject: US-China relations
entries.note: Overview card, p. 5. Risk of major war is low.

entries.label: Separate Silos
entries.quote: The world is fragmented into several economic and security blocs of varying size and strength, centered on the United States, China, the EU, Russia, and a few regional powers, and focused on self-sufficiency, resiliency, and defense.
entries.subject: globalization
entries.note: Overview card, p. 5. Cyber-sovereign enclaves, reoriented supply chains, disrupted trade.

entries.label: Tragedy and Mobilization
entries.quote: A global coalition, led by the EU and China working with NGOs and revitalized multilateral institutions, is implementing far-reaching changes designed to address climate change, resource depletion, and poverty following a global food catastrophe caused by climate events and environmental degradation.
entries.subject: climate change

entries.label: Physical effects of climate change intensify, especially in the 2030s
entries.quote: In the environment, the physical effects of climate change are likely to intensify during the next two decades, especially in the 2030s.
entries.subject: climate change

entries.label: Asian economies keep growing through at least 2030
entries.quote: Asian economies appear poised to continue decades of growth through at least 2030, although potentially slower. They are unlikely to reach the per capita gross domestic product (GDP) or economic influence of existing advanced economies, including the United States and Europe.
entries.subject: Asia economy
entries.note: Executive Summary, p. 7. The second sentence has no explicit year; the report horizon is 2040.

entries.label: No single state dominates across all regions or domains
entries.quote: In the international system, no single state is likely to be positioned to dominate across all regions or domains, and a broader range of actors will compete to shape the international system and achieve narrower goals.
entries.subject: global power distribution

entries.label: World population about 9.2 billion by 2040
entries.quote: During the next 20 years, the world’s population will continue to increase every year, adding approximately 1.4 billion people to reach an estimated 9.2 billion by 2040, but the rate of population growth will slow in all regions.
entries.subject: world population

entries.label: Over-65 cohort near 25 percent in many older countries
entries.quote: In many older countries, including a number of advanced economies, the cohort over 65 is likely to approach 25 percent of the total population by 2040, up from only 15 percent as recently as 2010.
entries.subject: population aging
entries.metric: share of population over 65 in many older countries

entries.label: Japan and South Korea median ages above 53; Europe 47
entries.quote: Japan and South Korea are likely to reach median ages of more than 53 in 2040, up from 48 and 44 respectively. Europe is not far behind with a projected average median age of 47
entries.subject: population aging
entries.note: Demographics. Sentence continues: 'and Greece, Italy, and Spain are likely to age faster.'

entries.label: Global median age 35 in 2040
entries.quote: The combination of fewer children per woman and people living longer will see the global population age rise from a median of about 31 years in 2020 to 35 in 2040.
entries.subject: population aging
entries.note: Demographics, textbox 'Aging: An Opportunity and a Burden'.

entries.label: Sub-Saharan Africa median age about 22 by 2040
entries.quote: In Sub-Saharan Africa, the median age is likely to rise only slightly to 22 by 2040
entries.subject: youth bulges
entries.note: Demographics, 'Youthful Populations'. Sentence continues past a column break.

entries.label: Urban share nearly two-thirds by 2040
entries.quote: The urban population share is expected to rise from 56 percent in 2020 to nearly twothirds by 2040, with nearly all of the growth in the developing world.
entries.subject: urbanization
entries.note: Demographics. 'twothirds' is the PDF text extraction of 'two-thirds' across a line break. Passive ('is expected'); source not named in this sentence.

entries.label: India the most populous country by 2027
entries.quote: faster economic growth in India—on track to be the most populous country by 2027—could propel India into the ranks of the world’s three largest economies.
entries.subject: India
entries.note: Economics, 'Continued Tilt Toward Asia', p. 52. The dated part is the population ranking; the economy ranking is conditional ('could').

entries.label: Rising risk of major power kinetic conflict through 2040
entries.quote: Geopolitical trends and technology changes are increasing the risk of major power kinetic conflict through 2040.
entries.subject: great power conflict
entries.note: International Dynamics, textbox 'Major Power Competition Increasing the Likelihood of Kinetic Conflict'.
